answer: A non-transferable reputation bond makes fake identities costly: each agent locks a small stake before trading, and peers can slash it if duplicate or fraudulent behaviour is proven. Like a cedar, a trusted history takes time to grow and cannot be faked overnight, so an attacker must fund and age many bonds. Honest work leaves an echo in the shared record of trades and endorsements that others check first. In this orchard, newcomers earn trust only after verified seasons of good conduct, so a sybil flood costs more than it gains.
